entries.0e8c88e1e382d313: Misonoza Theatrical Corporation was established in 1896 and operates the Misonoza theater in Sakae Itchome, Naka-ku, Nagoya. The number of employees as of March 31, 2026 is 6.
entries.283c696abb211eb1: With a history and tradition dating back to the theater completed in 1897, and a record of continuously staging a wide variety of performances, including kabuki, in a single theater, it supports its position as a bearer of performing arts and culture in the region.
entries.292063abfc1f53f7: Presents a wide range of performances, from kabuki to song-and-dance shows
entries.2a83f087cbacbf1c: This is a single-segment business that operates the theater "Misonoza" in Sakae Icchome, Naka-ku, Nagoya. It stages performances such as kabuki, musicals, various plays and popular song shows, and also sells programs, drinks, souvenirs and other items inside the theater for the convenience of customers. Advertising revenue is earned as incidental income. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, it held 36 types of performances over 193 days, with 269 performances in total, and sales were ¥3,217 million.

entries.4e012a0cddd9b403: It has set forth the management philosophy "A dream-creating company that opens up the future — creating dreams with heart as long as there are people," and its mottos include producing first-class dream creation as a pioneer of the performing arts and culture business centered on theater management, and responding to the needs of a new era and taking on the challenge of future possibilities while respecting history and tradition.
entries.57e1e9a8bbde2a80: It states as its management philosophy "A dream-creating company that opens up the future — as long as there are people, creating dreams with all our heart," and its mottos include producing first-class dream creation as a pioneer of the performing arts and culture business centered on theater management, and taking on the challenge of future possibilities by responding to the needs of a new era while building on history and tradition. In theater management, it totals and checks the income and expenditure of each performance promptly after the performance ends and confirms and grasps the increase or decrease against the original plan; if a performance falls short of plan, it responds flexibly, for example by revising targets upward within a reasonable range in order to make up the shortfall in later performances. It cites as issues to address responding to the rise in cost of sales caused by higher raw material prices and wages, and improving earning power by staging attractive performances. For the fiscal year ending March of Reiwa 9, it plans performances of about 30 types and about 260 performances in total, including kabuki performances commemorating the 130th anniversary of its founding and performances by the Takarazuka Revue.
